meanings.note: only when answering or making a phone call
Declinable neuter noun meaning 'dish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('platter') (large flat serving dish) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

examples.text: Осталось ровно три минуты до готовности блюда.
examples.trans: Exactly three minutes remain until the dish is ready.
The chef prepared a delicious dish.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: instrumental of вечер used as an adverb

examples.trans: I'm at home in the evening.

meanings.note: 'встретимся' = let's meet / we'll meet

examples.text: Аркаша, губернатор хочет с нами встретиться!
examples.trans: Arkasha, the governor wants to meet with us!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.
на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.en: to agree, to come to an arrangement
meanings.note: 'договоримся' = we'll work something out

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must, should; owe').

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to tremble', forming an aspectual pair with 'задрожать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Его руки немного дрожат от усталости.
examples.trans: His hands are shaking a bit from exhaustion.
Your face is pale, your hands are shaking a bit.
Why are you trembling so much?

meanings.note: Спасибо за + accusative. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.
+ instrumental. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'hello'.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Чн is pronounced шн. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: в кухне / на кухне = in the kitchen, на кухню = to the kitchen
E.g. русская кухня. Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.
We are sitting in the kitchen.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.
examples.trans: Come on in, please! As you can see, a big hall, and the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'car; machine' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'car; machine' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Which car did you come in?

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.
Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('molecular').

examples.trans: This is equipment for molecular cuisine.
Chef, will you look for a molecular cook?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Ну, папа!. Core Russian part meaning 'well; come on' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get, to receive', paired with 'получать'.

examples.text: А кто их получит? Те, кто сидит повыше?
examples.trans: And who will get it? The people who sit higher up?

meanings.en: to try, to have a go
meanings.note: + infinitive. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to try', paired with 'пробовать'.
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to try', paired with 'пробовать'.

examples.text: Как я могу это забыть? Ну, давай попробуем.
examples.trans: How can I forget that? Well, let's try.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пытаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to try, attempt'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и попытаться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to try on time.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'gift, present' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Have you already received my gift?

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть презент.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always gift.

meanings.en: to send (something or someone to the speaker)
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'слать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to send (here)', paired with 'присылать'.

examples.trans: They sent me a free lawyer.

examples.text: Послушайте, здесь ошибка. Ко мне прислали бесплатного адвоката. В чём дело?
examples.trans: Listen, there's a mistake here. They sent me a free lawyer. What's going on?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'демонстрировать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will demonstrate'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и продемонстрировать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and will demonstrate on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют продемонстрировать.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to will demonstrate.

meanings.note: Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: Жать руку = to shake hands. Common feminine noun meaning 'hand; arm' in everyday Russian.
+ instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Сколько стоит? = how much is it?. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cost; to be worth'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cost; to be worth'.

examples.trans: And how much does the console cost?

meanings.note: Hot liquid dish. Borrowed from French 'soupe' in the Petrine era.

examples.text: Сегодня на кухне сварили вкусный суп.
examples.trans: Today in the kitchen they cooked delicious soup.
I like hot soup very much!

examples.text: Мы добавим таблетку в её суп?
examples.trans: Shall we add the pill into her soup?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('edible').

examples.text: Называется съедобное меню, хочу у себя ввести.
examples.trans: It is called an edible menu, I want to introduce it at my place.

examples.text: О нашем новом съедобном меню, вы помните?
examples.trans: About our new edible menu, do you remember?

examples.text: Элеонора сказала, что нужно сделать съедобное меню.
examples.trans: Eleonora said that we need to make an edible menu.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('tomato').

examples.text: Хорошо! По вкусу просто томатный суп.
examples.trans: Good! By taste it is simply tomato soup.

meanings.note: 1st person singular future is not used by itself

examples.text: Ты его убедила? Ты уверена в этом?
examples.trans: You convinced him? Are you sure about this?

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: How something is done. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
As an answer. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
+ infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.
